as BZ_HUB_TOKEN_<NAME> and its `[[runner]]` to the host file. A running host starts it at its next start.

commit.help:
Worker: durably declare a git-commit artifact for REPO. Carries the ``git_commit``
kind only — an asset is declared through ``artifact create``. Node scope only. Echoes a
confirmation naming REPO, BRANCH, and the sha on success.

params.help: The leased environment the repo worktree lives in. Inferred while a chunk holds exactly one environment; required once it holds several.
params.name: environment_id

params.help: The repo's name in the environment's repo manifest (not an `owner/name` slug or URL). A name the manifest does not list is refused, naming the repos that are.
params.name: repo

params.help: The branch the commit was pushed to.
params.name: branch

params.help: The FULL commit sha (`git rev-parse HEAD`); an abbreviated sha fails verification against the pushed commit.
params.name: commit_sha

params.help: Always `node` — `graph` and `system` are read-only and refused.
params.name: scope

commit.short_help: Worker: durably declare a git-commit artifact for REPO.

create.help:
Worker: durably submit an asset artifact for a ``produces:`` NAME (content on stdin), node
scope only. A submission *stages* the content, published into the envelope only on completion
— read it back with ``artifact staged``. Empty stdin and any rejection exit
non-zero rather than silently losing the submission.

params.help: The `produces:` name this content is submitted for.
params.name: name

params.help: Always `node` — `graph` and `system` are read-only and refused.
params.name: scope

create.short_help: Worker: durably submit an asset artifact for a ``produces:`` NAME (content on stdin), node scope only.

get.help:
Worker: read one published artifact by NAME, passed literally, slashes included — a ``produces:`` name
(node scope), a baked-in graph declaration (graph scope), or one of blizzard's own published documents
(system scope). Refused when NAME is unknown, when more than one candidate matches (naming them), or when
this node-step has only staged it (pointing at ``artifact staged``). ``--content`` prints raw asset text,
refused for a git-commit artifact, which carries none.

params.help: The artifact's NAME, as an alternative to passing it positionally.
params.name: name_opt

params.help: The producing node's name, to disambiguate a NAME more than one node emits. Neither a graph declaration nor a system artifact has a producing node, so this narrows to node scope on its own — pairing it with `--scope graph`/`--scope system` is a contradiction and is refused.
params.name: node

params.help: Resolve NAME from one scope only — `node`, `graph`, or `system`. Omitted searches all three, and a NAME present in more than one is ambiguous the same as several producing nodes — unless `--node` settles it.
params.name: scope

params.help: Print the raw asset text to stdout instead of JSON (errors on a git-commit artifact).
params.name: content

get.short_help: Worker: read one published artifact by NAME, passed literally, slashes included — a ``produces:`` name (node scope), a baked-in graph declaration (graph scope), or one of blizzard's own published documents (system scope).

list.help:
Worker: list this node-step's artifacts as kind-discriminated JSON, resolved latest-by-epoch,
plus the graph mint's own baked-in declarations and blizzard's published system-artifact
set — ``--scope`` narrows to one. Content is elided by default; ``--content`` includes it.
Also includes this node-step's own staged, not-yet-published submissions,
each carrying ``"staged": true`` — everything published carries ``"staged": false``.

params.help: Include each artifact's full content instead of just its byte length.
params.name: content

params.help: Filter to one scope — `node` (this node-step's own artifacts), `graph` (the graph mint's baked-in declarations), or `system` (blizzard's own published documents). Omitted reads all three.
params.name: scope

list.short_help: Worker: list this node-step's artifacts as kind-discriminated JSON, resolved latest-by-epoch, plus the graph mint's own baked-in declarations and blizzard's published system-artifact set — ``--scope`` narrows to one.

staged.help:
Worker: list this node-step's own staged (not-yet-published) submissions, node scope only.
A fresh ``artifact create`` shows up here immediately; ``--content`` gives the full text.

params.help: Include each staged submission's full content instead of just its byte length.
params.name: content

params.help: Always `node` — `graph` and `system` hold no staged submission and are refused.
params.name: scope

staged.short_help: Worker: list this node-step's own staged (not-yet-published) submissions, node scope only.

artifact.help:
Worker: read node-step, graph, and system artifacts; write this node-step's own.
Every verb acts on this worker's own chunk — none names another. ``--scope`` picks node
scope, the graph mint's baked-in declarations, or blizzard's published system-artifact set.
``create`` *stages* a submission, published on completion.
artifact.short_help: Worker: read node-step, graph, and system artifacts; write this node-step's own.

asks.help:
Worker: read every question asked on this chunk, with its answer, as JSON — oldest-first,
open and answered alike, each row naming the asking node. A person's answer binds every later
session on the chunk: read this before asking again, and never contradict an answer.
asks.short_help: Worker: read every question asked on this chunk, with its answer, as JSON — oldest-first, open and answered alike, each row naming the asking node.

history.help:
Worker: read this chunk's own transition history as kind-discriminated JSON — the
merged, oldest-first timeline, one row per accepted transition, cross-graph migration, delivery
bounce, gate resolution, hub requeue, or restart, each carrying its own ``kind``. The in-flight
node-step this call is part of is not there yet: a transition is recorded only once an attempt completes.
history.short_help: Worker: read this chunk's own transition history as kind-discriminated JSON — the merged, oldest-first timeline, one row per accepted transition, cross-graph migration, delivery bounce, gate resolution, hub requeue, or restart, each carrying its own ``kind``.

notes.help:
Worker: read every note a person left on this chunk resolving a gate, requeueing it, or
restarting it, as JSON — oldest-first, each row carrying its ``kind`` and who left it. A
person's note binds every later session on the chunk as an answer does: never contradict one.
notes.short_help: Worker: read every note a person left on this chunk resolving a gate, requeueing it, or restarting it, as JSON — oldest-first, each row carrying its ``kind`` and who left it.

host.help:
Run the blizzard host until stopped: each runner works its chunks, and its local API answers `runner` verbs.

DIRECTORY (positional) and --dir are equivalent — pass one; giving both requires
they agree. Defaults to $BZ_RUNNER_DIR, then the cwd. A directory that has not graduated to a host is
refused, naming the graduation procedure.

ingest.help:
Move one runner from SOURCE — another host's directory, a `store reset --runner` archive, or a runner directory
that has not graduated — into this host:
its rows, its workspace, subscription and `[[runner]]` where this host lacks them, and its token; then delete its
rows from SOURCE, moving a source left with no runner aside. An archive's `[[runner]]` and token must already be
here. Refused while either host runs, or the hub does not hold the runner under this host; a re-run completes an
interrupted ingest.

params.help: Host directory (overrides $BZ_RUNNER_DIR).
params.name: directory

params.name: runner

params.name: workspace_id

init.help:
Scaffold the host file + data dir + a migrated store under DIRECTORY, then register the host at its hub and
join each of its runners under it. Idempotent.

A host token the hub knows — $BZ_HOST_TOKEN, the host file's `host_token`, then DIRECTORY/.env — keeps its host.
Holding none, the host is added at the hub under your `blizzard hub login` session when you hold one, in the
tenant --tenant names or else the only one you may enter, named after its first `[[runner]]`; its token is
written to DIRECTORY/.env as BZ_HOST_TOKEN. A runner holding no token is added under the host, its token
written to DIRECTORY/.env as BZ_HUB_TOKEN_<NAME> and its id to its `[[runner]]`; a runner whose token the hub
knows is kept when it stands under the host. A held token in another tenant than --tenant names stops: neither
a host nor a runner moves between tenants. A fresh host serves the projects --project names, else `default`. A
directory a pre-host runner left behind is refused, naming graduation, unless --allow-readd sets its store
aside. DIRECTORY defaults to $BZ_RUNNER_DIR, then the cwd.

params.help: The hub a fresh config names (overrides $BZ_HUB_URL).
params.name: hub_url

params.help: Add the host, or a runner, again when its hub does not know its token — only after that hub's data was reset. A host added again sets the store aside and adds every runner again under it; a runner beside another is never added again in place, since the store it would set aside is theirs too.
params.name: allow_readd

params.help: Add the host and its runners in this tenant, by id; needed only when you may enter several.
params.name: tenant_id

params.help: A project the runner serves, by id or slug; repeat for several. Default: `default` in a fresh config.
params.name: projects

init.short_help: Scaffold the host file + data dir + a migrated store under DIRECTORY, then register the host at its hub and join each of its runners under it.

migrate.help:
Apply or reverse migrations, or inspect this build's migration tree.

A directory that has not graduated to a host is refused and left as it is. A graduated one holding a pre-host
`data/runner.db` and no `data/host.db` adopts that store first. Adoption and --down hold the directory and are
refused while a host is running; a plain upgrade is refused only while a pre-host daemon answers.

Pause this runner: it starts no new workers until ``blizzard runner start``, and works with the hub
unreachable. Running workers are left alone — this is not a drain — but while paused a stalled worker is not
killed and an exhausted retry budget does not escalate. Separate from a pause set at the hub; each is cleared
where it was set.

Hand a needs_human chunk back to this runner after a human has worked it: one more try at its current
node, with its retry budget carried over. The runner keeps its claim, so the chunk never returns to the
hub's queue. Refused while a takeover of the chunk is open, when the chunk is not needs_human, or when
this runner holds no environment for it; repeating a pending requeue changes nothing.

`[[runner]]` from the host file. A running host stops running it shortly after.

releases them.

start.help:
Clear the pause ``blizzard runner pause`` set: this runner starts new workers again.

reset.help:
Move the store under DIRECTORY aside under a timestamped name, then migrate a fresh one; nothing is deleted.

With --runner, that runner's rows move to an archive store beside the host's, which `runner ingest` takes back,
and its outbox counters stay. Refused while the host holds the directory or a pre-host daemon answers on its
socket, and for a store that is not a SQLite file. DIRECTORY defaults to $BZ_RUNNER_DIR, then the cwd.

takeover.help:
Take over a chunk this runner holds: resume its session interactively in this terminal. The runner
leaves the chunk alone until the session exits, and an interrupted session still ends the takeover.
Refused when this runner holds no environment for the chunk, a takeover is already open, there is no
session to resume, a worker is running (unless ``--force``), or its result is still waiting to reach
the hub.

tick.help:
Run one pass of the host's runner against the live hub and workspace, then exit.

While a host serves the directory, the pass is stepped on that host over its socket, by the runner --runner
names or the host's only one; --host steps the host-wide pass instead. Exits 0 only when the pass completed.
With no host serving, the pass runs here: refused on a store revision mismatch, like ``host``, while another
process holds the directory, or while any of the host's runners is halted.

Re-read SEGMENT_ID's session and ship it again under a new segment id.

For a segment the hub holds in a form this runner has outgrown — most often one an older,
smaller per-record cap shrank. The hub never overwrites an accepted record, so superseding
one means a second segment: BOTH then show on the board. Same operating rules as `backfill`.
